A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same semantic-grounding feedback study. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial changes in title, organization, and layout.

before.justification: V1 reports original ADE20k and COCO experiments measuring grounding accuracy, feedback quality, and iterative correction across four VLMs.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds GPT-4o results, a human audit of label mapping, initial-prompt comparisons, and a cost analysis.

M1.justification: The same-VLM binary verifier, visual prompting, and iterative prediction-revision procedure remain unchanged. The self-correction terminology, reformatted prompt examples, and additional GPT-4o evaluation do not establish a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate region-to-class semantic grounding on ADE20k-150 and COCO panoptic segmentation. The added experiments and mapping audit use the existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The main iterative comparators remain intrinsic self-correction and oracle verification, renamed from noise-free verification. V2 additionally compares bounding-box base predictions against SoM and RoI-crop alternatives in Section 5.1, adding limited comparison controls.

E3.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o under the three-round proprietary-model evaluation, alternative initial-prompt settings, and a mapping audit of 100 outputs judged by one author. Existing dataset splits, grounding and feedback metrics, and open-model sampling settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 substantially broadens diagnostic analyses: Section 5.1 tests whether initial visual prompts weaken base predictions, Appendix B audits label-mapping errors, and Appendix C compares cost against accuracy. Existing feedback-prompt ablations, the F1-versus-accuracy correlation analysis, and qualitative failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Both implementation appendices specify averaging over three seeds, with proprietary-model experiments excepted. V2 introduces no confidence intervals, significance tests, error bars, or revised repeated-run policy. The reported Spearman correlations remain unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o trajectories, mapping-audit counts, initial-prompt scores, verification accuracies, and cost results. GPT-4o reaches 41.18 on ADE20k and 47.92 on COCO with VLM verification; its intrinsic self-correction also improves. Original four-model iterative entries are unchanged. V2 newly misattributes the 61.06-point class-label gain to LLaVA-1.5 in Section 4.1 and Table 1's caption; the tables assign that gain to CogVLM.

T1.justification: The semantic-grounding definitions and assumptions are retained. V1's explicit feedback-conditioned notation is replaced by prose without changing its mathematical substance. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim that prompted binary self-feedback improves grounding without retraining remains. V2 updates the headline automated improvement from approximately 5 to 8.4 points and adds a main finding that GPT-4V and GPT-4o retain over 40% ADE20k error after three oracle-feedback rounds.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting poor initial visual-prompt performance to bounding-box training and acknowledges uncertainty about GPT-4V/GPT-4o differences because their architectures and training data are unknown. Mapping ambiguity receives empirical support. V1's specific limitation concerning simultaneous feedback over multiple image regions is omitted.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies two A40 GPUs, GPT-4V/GPT-4o endpoint identifiers, and cosine-similarity mapping details. Existing checkpoint links and sampling parameters remain. V1's project website and code-access links are omitted; this establishes a disclosure change, not actual code withdrawal.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises positioning around the self-correction debate, adding the Kamoi survey, Chain-of-Verification, RARR, Reflexion, and supervised and reinforcement-learning approaches. It explicitly connects binary verification to decomposing difficult generation tasks into simpler verification tasks, while retaining much of the prompting and multimodal-evaluation background.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, research-question presentation, results discussion, and conclusion around self-correction. The four-question presentation becomes two main questions with subsidiary aspects, and the appendices are reorganized with a contents section.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout. V1 Table 1 is split into v2 Tables 1–2; iterative tables gain GPT-4o blocks; Tables 6–7 and the cost plot are added. Dialogue illustrations move into the appendix, and prompt templates receive substantially different formatting.

improvement.justification: V1 discussed mapping noise and compute costs qualitatively; v2 adds a 100-output audit and cost–accuracy curve, alongside initial-prompt controls and GPT-4o tests. These provide a modest improvement in evidence and transparency. Benefits are moderated by unresolved mapping errors, omitted project/code links, and the new misattribution of the 61.06-point gain in Section 4.1 and Table 1.
